questions.q: What does NULL represent in Oracle SQL?
questions.explain: NULL means the value is unknown or absent — it is distinct from zero or an empty string.

questions.q: Why does `WHERE vendor_site_id = NULL` silently return zero rows, even on rows that actually have a NULL there?
options: It raises a syntax error instead
Oracle automatically converts it to IS NULL behind the scenes
vendor_site_id can never actually be NULL
NULL is never equal to anything, including another NULL, so the `=` comparison is never true
questions.explain: NULL fails every equality comparison, including against itself, so `= NULL` never matches — the correct test is IS NULL.

questions.q: What does `NVL(discount_amount_taken, 0)` return when discount_amount_taken is NULL?
questions.explain: NVL substitutes the second argument (0) whenever the first argument is NULL.

questions.q: What is the key difference between NVL and NVL2?
options: NVL2 only works on numbers, NVL only works on text
There is no difference — they are aliases for the same function
NVL2 picks between two different replacement values depending on whether the expression is NULL; NVL only supplies one replacement for the NULL case
NVL2 is Oracle-specific; NVL is ANSI-standard
questions.explain: NVL2(expr, value_if_not_null, value_if_null) returns one of two values based on nullness; NVL only substitutes a replacement when the value is NULL.

questions.q: Why might a consultant choose COALESCE over NVL in Oracle code?
options: COALESCE runs faster in every case
COALESCE is ANSI-standard SQL (portable across databases) and can accept more than two arguments
NVL has been removed from modern Oracle versions
COALESCE can only be used with dates, never numbers
questions.explain: COALESCE is the ANSI-standard equivalent, works across more database platforms, and supports more than two arguments checked left to right.
